title.value: Empirical Analysis of Model Selection for Heterogeneous Causal Effect Estimation
title.justification: The paper focuses on the problem of model selection in causal inference for conditional average treatment effect (CATE) estimation, performing an empirical study to analyze various surrogate model selection metrics.
title.quote: We study the problem of model selection in causal inference, specifically for conditional average treatment effect (CATE) estimation.

extractions.description: This paper provides an empirical analysis for model selection in causal inference, focusing specifically on CATE estimation. It evaluates a wide range of surrogate metrics used for model selection by benchmarking them across 78 datasets and proposes new strategies, including two-level model selection and causal ensembling, to enhance the model selection process. The study examines the effectiveness of 34 surrogate metrics for CATE estimation, using AutoML for tuning and generative modeling to ensure reliable benchmarks.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily revolves around the methodological aspect of model selection for causal inference rather than directly addressing any eco-responsible domain such as climate change or sustainability.
primary_category.quote: While in some situations we ... based on domain knowledge and application requirements, it is desirable to have a model-free approach for model selection.

secondary_categories.justification: As with the primary category, the paper does not address eco-responsible themes specifically. It is concerned with methodology in machine learning and statistics.
secondary_categories.quote: We conduct an extensive empirical analysis to benchmark the surrogate model selection metrics introduced in the literature, as well as the novel ones introduced in this work.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not focus on any of the sub-categories listed under the eco-responsible domains, as it is not framed within an eco-responsible context.
primary_sub_category.quote: Our analysis shows that metrics that incorporate doubly robust aspects significantly dominate the rest across all datasets.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: Like the primary sub-category, no specific sub-category applies as the paper is methodological in nature and does not address eco-responsible sub-domains directly.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: We ensure a fair comparison by tuning the hyperparameters associated with these metrics via AutoML, and provide more detailed trends by incorporating realistic datasets via generative modeling.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper addresses the specific methodological challenge of model selection in causal inference for CATE estimation, which doesn't fit into the pre-defined eco-responsible categories.
new_primary_category.quote: We conduct an extensive empirical analysis to benchmark the surrogate model selection metrics introduced in the literature, as well as the novel ones introduced in this work.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The sub-category reflects the focus on methodologies and techniques for estimating heterogeneous treatment effects, central to this paper’s exploration and proposed strategies.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We study the problem of model selection in causal inference, specifically for conditional average treatment effect (CATE) estimation.
